ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p531/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p531/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p531/r2.claim: Before أَنْ, a verb is suppressed, such as when this happened; Moses first tried to reconcile the men, then reached for the Copt, an enemy of both Moses and Israel because of ethnic and reformist conflict.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p531/r2.anchor: tried to verbally reconcile the two

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r1.claim: Although some assign the accusation to the Copt, the author rejects this: the killing was still secret and Copts did not regard Moses as a reformer; the Israelite exposed the secret.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r1.anchor: the Copts never regarded Moses (sws) to be a reformer

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r2.claim: جَبَّار means dictatorial or out of control; the Israelite called Moses tyrannical, illustrating how a mean person praises help but attacks the helper when restrained.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r2.anchor: one who is out of control

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r3.claim: The Israelite’s charge also implies that his people saw Moses as a hope for reform and setting affairs right.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r3.anchor: he was regarded by his nation to be a ray of hope

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p293/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p293/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p293/r5.claim: The apparent referent of له is the Israelite, whom Moses rebukes as a troublemaker for having caused the previous killing; an alternative takes the referent as the Copt, with the Israelite misunderstanding the rebuke.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p293/r5.anchor: الظاهر أن الضمير في له عائد على الذي إنك لغوي مبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p293/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p293/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p293/r6.claim: The Israelite, mistaking Moses' intention, asks whether he means to kill him as he killed a man yesterday; rumor identified Moses as the killer and reached Pharaoh, who ordered Moses' death. Another reading makes the Israelite the one about to strike.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p293/r6.anchor: وكان تعيين القائل القبطي قد خفي على الناس، فانتشر في المدينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r1.claim: A reading of يبطش has kasra on the ta for most readers and damma for Hasan and Abu Ja'far; لو after a preceding oath can introduce the conditional, with a poetic citation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يبطش، بكسر الطاء والحسن، وأبو جعفر: بضمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r2.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r2.claim: The tyrant is one who kills without right; al-Shaʿbi says killing two people makes a person a tyrant, whom the verse contrasts with the righteous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r2.anchor: وقال الشعبي: من قتل رجلين فهو جبار، يعني بغير حق

QASHANI:28:17-19/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:17-19/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:17-19/r4.claim: Fancy and imagination oppose the heart by accusing it of wanting tyranny rather than reform.
QASHANI:28:17-19/r4.anchor: إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين

QASHANI:28:17-19/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:17-19/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:17-19/r5.claim: The heart calls its companion deviant because intellect is captivated by fancy, unable to repel it, and needs the heart's help.

QASHANI:28:17-19/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:17-19/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:17-19/r6.claim: The heart could not complete its intended attack because fancy obstructed and condemned it, asking whether it would repeat yesterday's killing.
QASHANI:28:17-19/r6.anchor: وإنما أراد أن يبطش ولما تيسر له البطش، ومانعه وأنكر فعله

QASHANI:28:17-19/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:17-19/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:17-19/r7.claim: Fancy remains permitted until the Great Resurrection; while the heart is only at the youthful station of its intermediate resurrection, fancy hopes to mislead it.
QASHANI:28:17-19/r7.anchor: لم يذعن له شيطان الوهم لأنه من المنظرين إلى يوم القيامة الكبرى

QASHANI:28:17-19/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:17-19/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:17-19/r8.claim: Mere intellectual and practical perfection cannot restrain fancy's ascendancy before the heart reaches the spirit and annihilation in sainthood with divine attributes.
QASHANI:28:17-19/r8.anchor: فما دام القلب في مقام الفتوة متصفا بكمالاته في القيامة الوسطى يطمع هو في إغوائه

DURR-FULL:v6p399/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the man who asked Moses for help again was the same man who had sought his help the previous day.
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه} قال: هو صاحب موسى الذي استنصره بالأمس

DURR-FULL:v6p399/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r7.claim: Ikrima likewise says the man seeking help was the same person who had sought it earlier.
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: الذي استنصره: هو الذي استصرخه

DURR-FULL:v6p399/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r8.claim: Qatada defines calling for aid as seeking help and says the words for seeking victory and calling for help are equivalent.
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه} قال: الاستصراخ: الاستغاثة قال: والاستنصار والاستصراخ واحد

DURR-FULL:v6p399/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r9.claim: Qatada says the man thought Moses meant to kill him and cried out about the previous killing; a nearby Copt overheard and exposed them.
DURR-FULL:v6p399/r9.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه} قال: الاستصراخ: الاستغاثة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

MAJAZ:v2p99/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p99/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p99/r10.claim: Baṭasha with ṭāʾ kasra or ḍamma are two dialectal forms.

MUQATIL:28:16-19/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r6.claim: As Moses moves to strike the Egyptian, who is enemy to both him and the Israelite, the Israelite thinks Moses means to strike him because of the rebuke.
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r6.anchor: يعني عدوا لموسى وعدوا للإسرائيلى، ظن الإسرائيلي أن موسى يريد أن يبطش به

MUQATIL:28:16-19/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r7.claim: The Israelite asks whether Moses will kill him as he killed a person yesterday and accuses him of wanting to become a tyrant who kills unjustly rather than one of the reformers, the obedient to God.
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r7.anchor: يعني قتالا { في الأرض } مثل سيرة الجبابرة القتل في غير حق { وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين }

MUQATIL:28:16-19/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r8.claim: Egyptians did not know who had committed the killing until the Israelite exposed Moses; the Copt reported him, and they plotted to kill Moses.
MUQATIL:28:16-19/r8.anchor: ولم يكن أهل مصر علموا بالقاتل، حتى أفشى الإسرائيلي على موسى، فلما سمع القبطي بذلك انطلق، فأخبرهم أن موسى هو القاتل،

RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses omitted ‘if God wills’ from his promise not to help criminals and was therefore tested the following day.
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : لم يستثن ولم يقل فلن أكون ظهيرا إن شاء الله ، فابتلي به في اليوم الثاني

RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r8.claim: Rāzī calls Ibn ʿAbbās’s account weak: Moses refrained from aiding the man the next day; only the enemy feared he would become a tyrant.
RAZI-FULL:v24p201/r8.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لأنه في اليوم الثاني ترك الإعانة ، وإنما خاف منه ذلك العدو

TAB-FULL:v18p186/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r3.claim: In another report, the Israelite later appealed while fighting another man; the man recognized Moses as the killer from the previous day, and the news led to Moses fleeing.
TAB-FULL:v18p186/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: " {فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان} [القصص: 15] قال: رجل من بني إسرائيل يقاتل جبارا لفرعون فاستغاثه

TABATABAI:28:15-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15-21/r4.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:28:15-21/r4.claim: Al-Riḍā recounts Moses’ rebuke and intended chastisement of the Israelite for fighting again; the Israelite then accuses Moses of wanting to kill him as he killed a man the day before.
TABATABAI:28:15-21/r4.anchor: قاتلت رجلا بالأمس وتقاتل هذا اليوم لأؤدبنك

ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r3.claim: On Zajjaj’s grammatical reading, the Israelite seeking aid was trying to have Moses strike their shared enemy, but Moses did not do so and called the Israelite plainly misguided.
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r3.anchor: فلما أراد المستصرخ أن يبطش موسى بالذي

ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r4.claim: The Israelite exposed Moses’ earlier killing by revealing it to Pharaoh’s people.

ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r5.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r5.claim: A saying calls anyone who has killed two people a جبار.
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r5.anchor: ويقال إن من قتل اثنين فهو جبار

ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r6.claim: جبار means an arrogant person who will not humble himself before God; unjustly killing one or many people makes a killer a جبار.
ZAJJAJ:v4p137/r6.anchor: والجبار في اللغة المتعظم الذي لا يتواضع لأمر الله

TABRISI:28:17-20/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:17-20/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:17-20/r1.claim: “Waiting” means anticipating; “calling for help” means seeking an appeal against an enemy that will deter his attack.
TABRISI:28:17-20/r1.anchor: الترقب الانتظار والاستصراخ طلب الصراخ على العدو بما يردعه عن الإيقاع به

TABRISI:28:17-20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:17-20/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:17-20/r6.claim: In “when he intended to seize,” the first “an” is redundant; the second with its clause is the object of “intended.”
TABRISI:28:17-20/r6.anchor: أن الأولى زائدة وأن الثانية مع صلتها منصوبة الموضع بأنها مفعولة إرادة

TABRISI:28:17-20/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:17-20/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:17-20/r16.claim: The Israelite whom Moses rescued the day before cries out for help against another Copt with whom he is arguing.
TABRISI:28:17-20/r16.anchor: معناه أن الإسرائيلي الذي كان قد خلصه بالأمس ووكز القبطي من أجله يستصرخ موسى ويستعين به على رجل آخر من القبط خاصمه.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:17-21/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:17-21/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:17-21/r3.claim: Moses rebukes the Israelite for inviting him to another fight after yesterday's killing; when Moses approaches, the Israelite mistakes his target and says Moses wants to kill him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:17-21/r3.anchor: ظاهر الغواية، قد قتلت بك بالأمس رجلا، وتدعوني إلى آخر، وأقبل إليهما

RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r7.claim: One view makes the Israelite the speaker: after Moses called him misguided and angrily moved to strike, he thought Moses meant to kill him; only he knew of the previous killing, so he exposed it and increased Moses’ fear.
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم لما خاطب موسى الإسرائيلي بأنه غوي ورآه على غضب ظن لما هم بالبطش

RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r8.claim: The other view makes the Copt the speaker, already informed by the Israelite; Rāzī prefers it because the next clause’s “tyrant on earth” accusation suits an unbeliever, and the verse attributes the speech to the enemy of both.
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r8.anchor: قول القبطي ، وقد كان عرف القصة من الإسرائيلي

RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r9.claim: One definition of jabbār is someone who unjustly does whatever he wants by beating and killing, without considering consequences or choosing the better response.
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r9.anchor: الجبار الذي يفعل ما يريد من الضرب والقتل بظلم لا ينظر في العواقب

RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r10.claim: Another definition is an arrogant person who will not submit to anyone’s command.
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r10.anchor: وقيل المتعظم الذي لا يتواضع لأمر أحد

RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r11.claim: After this incident, the news spread through the city, reached Pharaoh, and they resolved to kill Moses.
RAZI-FULL:v24p202#2/r11.anchor: ولما وقعت هذه الواقعة انتشر الحديث في المدينة وانتهى إلى فرعون وهموا بقتله

BURSEVI:v6p285/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r4.claim: Baṭsh means taking or seizing something with force.

BURSEVI:v6p285/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r5.claim: Moses meant to seize the Copt, enemy to both men because he was not of their faith and Egyptians generally opposed Israelites.
BURSEVI:v6p285/r5.anchor: أي يأخذ بيد القبطي الذي هو عدو لموسى والإسرائيلي إذ لم يكن على دينهما ولأن القبط كانوا أعداء بني إسرائيل على الإطلاق.

BURSEVI:v6p285/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r6.claim: The speaker may be the Israelite, who thinks Moses is about to attack him because of the rebuke and angry look, or the Copt, who suspects Moses is yesterday’s killer after hearing their remark.
BURSEVI:v6p285/r6.anchor: {قال} ذلك الإسرائيلي ظانا أن موسى يريد أن يبطش به

BURSEVI:v6p285/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r7.claim: An alternative makes the Copt the speaker, supposing from their words that Moses killed the Copt the previous day for the Israelite.
BURSEVI:v6p285/r7.anchor: أو قال القبطي ، وكأنه توهم من قولهم أنه الذي قتل القبطي بالأمس لهذا الإسرائيلي.

BURSEVI:v6p285/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r8.claim: In means ‘you only want’; a tyrant does what he wishes without considering consequences, unlike a reformer who settles disputes.
BURSEVI:v6p285/r8.anchor: {إن تريد} أي : ما تريد {إلا أن تكون جبارا فى الأرض} وهو الذي يفعل ما يريده من الضرب والقتل

BURSEVI:v6p285/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r9.claim: The accusation is that Moses does not intend to reconcile people and end their quarrels.
BURSEVI:v6p285/r9.anchor: {وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين} بين الناس بالقول والفعل فتدفع التخاصم

BURSEVI:v6p285/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r10.claim: The accusation spread to Pharaoh and his council; since the Israelite alone knew the killing was Moses’ deed, they resolved to kill him, and his believing cousin came to warn him.
BURSEVI:v6p285/r10.anchor: ولما قال هذا انتشر الحديث وارتقى إلى فرعون وملئه وظهر أن القتل الواقع أمس صدر من موسى

STUDYQURAN:28:19/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r1.claim: The words accusing Moses of murder are usually understood to be spoken by the Egyptian enemy.
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r1.anchor: These words are usually thought to be spoken by the enemy

STUDYQURAN:28:19/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r2.claim: Some instead attribute the words to the Israelite whom Moses had helped earlier.
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r2.anchor: some say they could also be spoken by the Israelite whom Moses had helped previously

STUDYQURAN:28:19/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r3.claim: On the alternative reading, the Israelite’s words exposed the previous day’s incident and led to Moses’ flight.
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r3.anchor: According to this latter reading, it was this statement that exposed the incident from the day before, which led to Moses’ flight

STUDYQURAN:28:19/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī explains jabbār as someone who violently oppresses without regard for consequences or seeking the best way to act.
STUDYQURAN:28:19/r4.anchor: Here tyrant renders jabbār, which al-Rāzī explains is a human being who commits violence and oppression

TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r1.claim: Moses meant to strike the Egyptian, who was an enemy to both him and the Israelite; the Israelite mistakenly thought Moses meant to strike him.
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r1.anchor: قال الإسرائيلي لموسى وظن أنه إياه يريد

TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r2.claim: The Israelite feared Moses after Moses called him clearly misguided.
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " {فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما قال} [القصص: 19] : خافه الذي من شيعته

TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r3.claim: After Moses rebuked the Israelite and approached the Egyptian to help him, the Israelite feared Moses because of the harsh rebuke, accused him, and Moses left him.
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r3.anchor: عن السدي: " قال موسى للإسرائيلي: {إنك لغوي مبين} [القصص: 18] ثم أقبل لينصره

TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r4.claim: His companions report that Moses regretted the previous killing, then rebuked the Israelite before approaching another Egyptian; the Israelite mistook Moses’ intent and recalled the prior killing.
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عبد الله، عن أصحابه، قال: " ندم بعد أن قتل القتيل

TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r5.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r5.claim: Moses regretted the killing and wished he had not struck either man; when he stopped the Israelite from attacking the Egyptian, the Israelite feared him and exposed the earlier killing, which the Egyptian spread.
TAB-FULL:v18p195#2/r5.anchor: وهو في الكتاب ابن أبي نجيح: " أن موسى لما أصبح، أصبح نادما تائبا

TAB-FULL:v18p197/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r1.claim: A tyrant’s conduct includes killing people unjustly, without lawful cause.
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r1.anchor: وكان من فعل الجبابرة: قتل النفوس ظلما، بغير حق

TAB-FULL:v18p197/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r2.claim: One explanation is that the Israelite called Moses a tyrant because their convention treated someone who killed two people as a tyrant.
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r2.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال ذلك لموسى الإسرائيلي لأنه كان عندهم: من قتل نفسين من الجبابرة

TAB-FULL:v18p197/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r3.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says that whoever kills two men is a tyrant.
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي، قال: " من قتل رجلين فهو جبار؛ قال: ثم قرأ

TAB-FULL:v18p197/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r4.claim: Qatāda says tyrants kill a person without that person having killed anyone.
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r4.anchor: عن قتادة: " {إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض} [سورة: القصص، آية رقم: 19] إن الجبابرة هكذا

TAB-FULL:v18p197/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj calls killing one person in exchange for no killing the way of tyrants.
TAB-FULL:v18p197/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج، " {إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض} [سورة: القصص، آية رقم: 19] قال: تلك سيرة الجبابرة

TAB-FULL:v18p198/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p198/r1.claim: The reformers are those who work for the good of the earth’s people through obedience to God.
TAB-FULL:v18p198/r1.anchor: {وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين} [سورة: القصص، آية رقم: 19] أي ما هكذا يكون الإصلاح

TAB-FULL:v18p198/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p198/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses the accusation as saying that this is not how reform is done.
TAB-FULL:v18p198/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين} [سورة: القصص، آية رقم: 19] أي ما هكذا يكون الإصلاح

TAB-FULL:v18p199/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p199/r1.speaker: معمر
TAB-FULL:v18p199/r1.claim: Maʿmar reports that a nearby Egyptian heard the Israelite remind Moses of the previous killing and spread the remark.
TAB-FULL:v18p199/r1.anchor: عن معمر، قال: " قال الإسرائيلي لموسى: {أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس} [القصص: 19] وقبطي قريب منهما

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r1.speaker: جل المفسرين
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r1.claim: Most exegetes say the Israelite whom Moses had come to help spoke the accusation: frightened by Moses’ anger at his earlier conduct, he feared Moses meant to strike him.
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r1.anchor: ذكر جل المفسرين أن ضمير { قال } للإسرائيلي الذي كان يستصرخه وذلك أنه ظن أن موسى إنما يريد

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r2.claim: Tabataba’i accepts the Israelite as speaker on contextual grounds and rejects the claim that the Copt spoke; the Israelite’s words revealed Moses as yesterday’s killer, prompting the Copt to inform Pharaoh and the plot to kill Moses.
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r2.anchor: وما ذكروه في محله لشهادة السياق بذلك فلا يعبأ بما قيل إن القائل هو القبطي دون الإسرائيلي

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r3.claim: Calling the Copt an enemy to both men implicitly contradicts the present Torah’s claim that both fighters were Israelites, and supports the Israelite as the speaker.
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r3.anchor: وفي قوله { أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما } تعريض للتوراة الحاضرة حيث تذكر أن المتقاتلين هذين كانا جميعا إسرائيليين

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r8.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r8.claim: A report in Tafsīr al-Qummī says Moses had been honored at Pharaoh’s court until adulthood; after killing Pharaoh’s follower while defending an Israelite, he hid, then fled when another Israelite repeated the accusation.
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r8.anchor: فلم يزل موسى عند فرعون في أكرم كرامة حتى بلغ مبلغ الرجال

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r9.speaker: علي بن محمد بن الجهم
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r9.claim: In a report from the meeting of al-Maʾmūn and al-Riḍā, al-Maʾmūn asks whether al-Riḍā holds that prophets are infallible, and al-Riḍā affirms it.
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r9.anchor: بإسناده إلى علي بن محمد بن الجهم قال حضرت مجلس المأمون وعنده الرضا عليه السلام فقال له المأمون

TABRISI:28:18-20/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:18-20/r3.claim: Moses felt compassion for the Israelite and meant to seize and repel their Egyptian enemy; the Israelite mistook Moses’ rebuke as a threat to himself.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r3.anchor: فلما أخذته الرقة على الإسرائيلي وأراد أن يدفع القبطي

TABRISI:28:18-20/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:28:18-20/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most exegetes say the Israelite spoke, thinking Moses meant to attack him.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r4.anchor: بالأمس عن ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:28:18-20/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r5.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:28:18-20/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan instead says the Egyptian spoke, since the killing had become widely known and he thought an Israelite had killed the man the day before.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو من قول القبطي لأنه قد اشتهر أمر القتل بالأمس

TABRISI:28:18-20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:18-20/r6.claim: Here a jabbār is one who seeks dominance through killing and oppression.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r6.anchor: أي ما تريد إلا أن تكون عاليا في الأرض بالقتل والظلم

TABRISI:28:18-20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r7.speaker: عكرمة والشعبي
TABRISI:28:18-20/r7.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Shaʿbī say a person is called a tyrant only after killing two people unjustly.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r7.anchor: قال عكرمة والشعبي: لا يكون الإنسان جبارا حتى يقتل نفسين بغير حق

TABRISI:28:18-20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:18-20/r8.claim: The Egyptian recognized Moses as the killer, informed Pharaoh, and Pharaoh ordered Moses killed and sent men to find him.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r8.anchor: علم القبطي أن القاتل موسى فانطلق إلى فرعون وأخبر به

THALABI:v7p242/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p242/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses reached to strike the Egyptian; the Israelite saw his anger, feared he meant to kill him, and accused him, though Moses meant the Egyptian.
THALABI:v7p242/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثم مد موسى يده وهو يريد أن يبطش بالفرعوني، فنظر الإسرائيلي إلى موسى

THALABI:v7p242/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p242/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses becoming a tyrant in the land as killing unjustly.
THALABI:v7p242/r3.anchor: إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض بالقتل ظلما

THALABI:v7p242/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r4.speaker: عكرمة والشعبي
THALABI:v7p242/r4.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Shaʿbi say a person is not a tyrant until he has unjustly killed two people.
THALABI:v7p242/r4.anchor: قال عكرمة والشعبي: لا يكون الإنسان جبارا حتى يقتل نفسين بغير حق.

THALABI:v7p242/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p242/r5.claim: After the accusation, the two men separated; the Egyptian understood from the Israelite's words that Moses had killed the earlier Egyptian, informed Pharaoh, and Pharaoh ordered Moses's death.
THALABI:v7p242/r5.anchor: فلما سمع القبطي ما قال الإسرائيلي علم أن موسى قتل ذلك الفرعوني، فانطلق إلى فرعون،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r1.claim: The Israelite thought Moses meant to strike the Egyptian, because he had accused him of being openly misguided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r1.anchor: فقال: {يا موسى أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس} وهذا قول جميع المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r2.claim: They say no one knew Moses had killed the Egyptian until the Israelite exposed him; the Egyptian heard, learned who the killer was, and informed Pharaoh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس والكلبي: ولم يكن أحد اطلع ولا علم أن موسى هو الذي قتل القبطي بالأمس، حتى أفشى عليه الإسرائيلي أنه هو القاتل بالأمس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r3.claim: Exegetes say Moses was tested for not making an exception: the next day he faced a similar situation, nearly struck again, and his previous killing became known, forcing him to flee.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r3.anchor: والذي قاله المفسرون: إنه لم يستثن فابتلي، هو هذا، وهو أنه وقع من الغد في مثل ما وقع بالأمس، وهم بالبطش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r4.claim: The exegetes gloss “tyrant in the land” as fighting people through oppression.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq defines a jabbar as an arrogant person who will not submit to God’s command; an unjust killer is also called a jabbar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p362/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: الجبار في اللغة: المتعظم الذي لا يتواضع لأمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq says that this is not what reform looks like.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي ما هكذا يكون الإصلاح

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r4.claim: The one who was an enemy to both men was the Egyptian Copt.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r4.anchor: {فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما} [القصص: 19] بالقبطي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r5.claim: The speaker who calls out to Moses is the Israelite.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r6.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r6.claim: Yaḥyā reports hearing that the Israelite was the Samaritan; the following clause is cut off in this segment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584/r6.anchor: قال يحيى: بلغني أنه السامري، وخلى السامري عن القبطي و

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r1.claim: The Israelite is the one who says “O Moses.”

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r2.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī explains Moses’ alleged tyranny as being a killer in the land.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r2.anchor: {أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا} [القصص: 19] ، أي: قتالا. {في الأرض} [القصص: 19] وهو تفسير السدي.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:18/r1.claim: Because the Egyptian’s killer was not yet known, Moses spent the night fearing consequences; the next day he found the same Israelite fighting another Egyptian, scolded him as a troublemaker, then tried to strike the Egyptian, whom the Israelite feared Moses would hit him instead.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:18/r1.anchor: Mûsâ dün başını belâya sokmuş olan İsrâilli’yi, “Doğrusu sen azgının birisin” diyerek azarladı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:18/r2.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:18/r2.claim: Some commentators attribute the accusation to the Egyptian, who had already learned from the Israelite who had killed the previous day’s victim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:18/r2.anchor: Konuşmanın akışına bakarak bu sözün Kıptî’ye ait olduğunu söyleyenler de vardır. Bunlara göre Kıptî olayın fâilini daha önce İsrâilli’den öğrenmişti (bk. Şevkânî, IV, 159)

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r1.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r1.claim: It is said the man did not know Moses had killed the Egyptian the day before; seeing Moses intervene for his companion, he inferred Moses was the killer.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r1.anchor: قيل لم يعلم ذلك الرجل أن موسى هو الذي قتل الرجل بالأمس ، ولكن لما قصد منعه عن صاحبه استدل

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r2.claim: The man's words spread among people as news that Moses had killed the Egyptian, and Moses then refrained from the man.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r2.anchor: فلما ذكر ذلك شاع في أفواه الناس أن موسى هو الذي قتل القبطي بالأمس ، فأمسك موسى عن هذا الرجل

BURHAN:v1p133/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p133/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p133/r8.claim: The construction فلما أن occurs twice: in Yūsuf when the bearer of good news arrives and in al-Qaṣaṣ when Moses is about to strike.
BURHAN:v1p133/r8.anchor: ﴿ فلما أن ﴾ حرفان فى يوسف ﴿ فلما أن جاء البشير ﴾ وفى القصص ﴿ فلما أن أراد أن يبطش ﴾

BURHAN:v3p13/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p13/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p13/r1.claim: In 28:19, repeating أن within the action clause adds emphasis.
BURHAN:v3p13/r1.anchor: كررت أن في أربع مواضيع تأكيدا

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

ITQAN:v3p93/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p93/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p93/r1.claim: One scholar divides Qur'anic address into three kinds: speech fitting only the Prophet, only others, or both.
ITQAN:v3p93/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم خطاب القرآن ثلاثة أقسام قسم لا يصح إلا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v3p93/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p93/r2.speaker: ابن القيم
ITQAN:v3p93/r2.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says Qur'anic address depicts God as sovereign, guides with praise, counsel, promise, warning and proof, recounts friends' and enemies' ends, calls to Paradise, warns of Hell, stresses human dependence, God's justice, mercy and tender care for favorites.
ITQAN:v3p93/r2.anchor: قال ابن القيم تأمل خطاب القرآن تجد ملكا له الملك كله وله الحمد كله أزمة الأمور كلها بيده

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r1.claim: True wealth is freedom from need; a rich person whose greed keeps generating new wants remains needy, like the glutton who eats but is never satisfied.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r1.anchor: حقيقة الغنى هو انتفاء الحاجة والحاجة أن تريد الشيء ولا تجده

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r2.claim: A miser may be unable to use the wealth he owns; real wealth requires generosity, sound judgment, and resolve to control and spend one’s possessions, as al-Buhturi’s verse illustrates.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r2.anchor: لأنه عدم كرما يبسط أنامله وجودا ينصر آمله وعقلا ينصره وهمة تمكنه مما لديه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r3.claim: Custom calls abundant money wealth and little money poverty because money tends to satisfy wants, but this names the cause for its effect; the true meanings are absence and presence of need.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r3.anchor: فهو من جنس تسمية السبب باسم المسبب وإلا فحقيقة الغنى انتفاء الاحتياج وحقيقة الفقر الاحتياج

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r4.claim: God alone is truly rich, since need is impossible for Him and He is exalted above the attributes of created beings.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r4.anchor: والله تعالى الغنى على الحقيقة لاستحالة الاحتياج عليه جل وتعالى عن صفات المخلوقين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r5.speaker: رسول الله
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r5.claim: The Prophet distinguishes worldly insolvency from the true bankrupt person: one arrives with worship but has wronged others, whose claims consume his good deeds before their sins are placed on him.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r5.anchor: رسول الله قال أتدرون ما المفلس قالوا المفلس فينا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r6.claim: In the afterlife good deeds function like worldly wealth because they bring felicity and avert punishment; someone stripped of them is therefore truly bankrupt.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p66/r6.anchor: لما كان الإنسان إنما يعد غنيا في الدنيا بماله لأنه يجتلب به المسرة ويدفع المضرة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r1.claim: Some comparisons are wholly imaginary: ruby standards with emerald shafts and pearl vessels containing carnelian are not objects one encounters in reality, especially when the ruby is imagined unfurled.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r1.anchor: فليس في العادة أن تتخذ صورة أعلاها ياقوت على مقدار العلم وتحت ذلك الياقوت قطع مطاولة من الزبرجد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r2.claim: In the image of dawn throwing off its garment, the garment is moved aside to expose most of the body, not removed entirely; otherwise the comparison would concern dawn alone and clash with dawn appearing beneath night.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r2.anchor: في إلقاء الجل أن تريد أنه أداره عن ظهره وأزاله عن مكانه حتى تكشف أكثر جسده لا أنه رمى به جملة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r3.claim: The lightning and piebald image concerns a sudden flash, like white patches appearing when a horse leaps and its covering shifts, rather than a simple comparison of lightning’s color; Ibn Babak offers a parallel.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r3.anchor: ينبغي أن يكون الغرض بذكر الجل أن البرق يلمع بغتة ويلوح للعين فجأة فصار لذلك كبياض الأبلق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r4.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s “when it leapt” adds force, while an earlier poet’s prancing and circling horses preserve the chief basis of resemblance: their movement and the manner of the flash.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r4.anchor: وقد عنى المتقدمون أيضا بمثل هذا الاحتياط ألا تراه قال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r5.claim: The second kind of comparison depicts things that can exist, though some are common and others rare; the stars scattered like pearls on a blue carpet illustrate this kind.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p148/r5.anchor: هذا القسم الثاني الذي يدخل في الوجود يتفاوت حاله فمنه ما يتسع وجوده ومنه ما يوجد في النادر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r1.claim: Wordplay and rhymed prose succeed when the meaning leads the speaker to them; removing them would then make the expression awkward, unlike an effect imposed on the meaning.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r1.anchor: أن المتكلم لم يقد المعنى نحو التجنيس والسجع بل قادة المعنى إليهما وعبر به الفرق عليهما

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r2.claim: The soundest practice is to let meanings follow their own course and find fitting words; deciding in advance to pun or rhyme with chosen words risks affectation and error.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r2.anchor: أن ترسل المعاني على سجيتها وتدعها تطلب لانفسها الالفاظ فانها إذا تركت وما تريد لم تكنس إلا ما يليق بها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r3.claim: The naturally arising wordplay in the cited “أودعاني” line and Abu Tammam’s Najd and “الحمام” couplets shows how a meaning can happen to invite a pun.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r3.anchor: كما ساعد أبا تمام في نحو قوله ( وأنجدتم من بعد إتهام داركم فيا دمع أنجدني على ساكني نجد )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r4.claim: Abu Tammam treats every place-name as an obligation to devise a pun, producing contrived examples; such forced wordplay, like the later poet’s “داء” conceit, invites criticism.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p10/r4.anchor: أسلم نفسه للتكلف ويرى انه إن مر على اسم موضع يحتاج إلى ذكره أو يتصل بقصة يذكرها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r1.claim: Kināya conveys an intended attribute indirectly by naming a consequence that accompanies it, as tall stature by a long sword strap or hospitality by abundant cooking ash.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r1.anchor: فقد أرادوا في هذا كله كما ترى معنى ، ثم لم يذكروه بلفظه الخاص به ، ولكنهم توصلوا إليه بذكر معنى آخر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r2.claim: He treats the best-known forms of figurative expression as استعارة and تمثيل, with تمثيل counting as metaphor when it follows metaphor's pattern.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r2.anchor: والاسم والشهرة فيه لشيئين : الاستعارة والتمثيل . وإنما يكون التمثيل مجازا إذا جاء على حد الاستعارة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r3.claim: Metaphor substitutes the comparison's image for an explicit simile; a second form instead attributes a nonexistent property, such as giving the north wind a hand.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p66/r3.anchor: ذاك أنك في الأول تجعل الشيء الشيء ليس به . وفي الثاني تجعل للشيء الشيء ليس له

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r1.claim: A negation followed by إلا can either deny that anyone besides Zayd came, or identify Zayd as the sole person who came; the focus differs.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r1.anchor: احتمل أمرين ؛ أحدهما : أن تريد اختصاص زيد بالمجيء ، وأن تنفيه عمن عداه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r2.claim: Jesus's statement means he did not omit the command to worship God or say its opposite, rather than merely claiming he added nothing beyond the command.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r2.anchor: ليس المعنى أني لم أزد على ما أمرتني به شيئا ، ولكن المعنى أني لم أدع ما أمرتني به أن أقوله لهم وقلت خلافه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r3.claim: In the cited verse, the exception identifies the one who felled the horseman as the speaker; it does not assert that nobody else shared in felling him.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r3.anchor: المعنى : أنا الذي قطر الفارس ، وليس المعنى على أنه يريد أن يزعم أنه انفرد بأن قطره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r4.claim: With إلا, fronting the object focuses who acted, while fronting the subject focuses who was acted upon; he illustrates the contrast with عمرو and زيد.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p258/r4.anchor: والفرق بينهما أنك إذا قلت : ما ضرب زيدا إلا عمر و ؛ فقدمت المنصوب كان الغرض بيان الضارب من هو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265/r1.claim: غير has the same interpretive possibilities as إلا: it may deny an accompanying person or deny that someone else came in Zayd's place.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265/r1.anchor: واعلم أن حكم ' غير ' في جميع ما ذكرنا حكم ' إلا ' ؛ فإذا قلعت : ما جاءني غير زيد ؛ احتمل أن تريد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265/r2.claim: The construction cannot append لا عمرو after ما جاءني غير زيد, just as it cannot after ما جاءني إلا زيد.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p265/r2.anchor: ولا يصح أن تقول : ما جاءني غير زيد لا عمر و . كما لم يجز : ما جاءني إلا زيد لا عمر و

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r1.claim: Although إنما can introduce information the listener did not know, it also implies that the point is especially disclosed and evident in the given context.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r1.anchor: فإنه لا بد مع ذلك من أن يدعى هناك فضل انكشاف وظهور في أن الأمر كالذي ذكر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r2.claim: In examples such as كان زيد and كان حليما, إنما introduces what the listener already expects from the construction: respectively its predicate or its subject.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r2.anchor: فالمخاطب ينتظر الخبر . وإذا قلت : كان حليما ، أنه ينتظر الاسم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r3.claim: After قلت, a quotation intended as meaning must be a complete sentence, not a bare word, unless the speaker intends to report the word's form itself.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r3.anchor: أنه معلوم أنك لا تحكي بعد ' قلت ' إذا كنت تنحو نحو المعنى ، إلا ما كان جملة مفيدة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r4.claim: When إنما appears to introduce wholly new information, contextual evidence is already present, so the listener can infer the point at once.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p267/r4.anchor: فإن رأيتها قد دخلت على كلام هو ابتداء إعلام بشيء لم يعلمه السامع فلأن الدليل عليه حاضر منعه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r1.claim: The eloquence relevant to Qur'anic inimitability is an advantage reached through thought and reflection, not a property of isolated wording or sound arrangement.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r1.anchor: المزية المطلوبة في هذا الباب مزية فيما طريقه الفكر والنظر من غير شبهة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r2.claim: Ordinary inflection is not an eloquence advantage because Arabs share that knowledge; interpreting a figurative subject's agency requires thought but concerns the description that licenses the inflection.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r2.anchor: إن العلم بالإعراب مشترك بين العرب كلهم ، وليس هو مما يستنبط بالفكر ، ويستعان عليه بالروية

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r3.claim: Dialect preference, avoiding common mistakes, and using rare vocabulary are not the source of the Qur'an's eloquence, since these depend on memorized lexical knowledge.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r3.anchor: ومن ثم لا يجوز لنا أن نعتد في شأننا هذا بأن يكون المتكلم قد استعمل من اللغتين في الشيء ما يقال إنه أفصحهما

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r4.claim: Most Qur'anic words called rare are unusual because of metaphorical usage, not because the words themselves are obscure; genuinely rare vocabulary occurs only in a few cases.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p294/r4.anchor: إنما كان غريبا من أجل استعارة هي فيه كمثل : ( ﴿ وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل ﴾ ) ومثل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p304/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p304/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p304/r1.claim: A speaker does not aim to teach dictionary definitions of individual words; meaning arises from how the words are related in the sentence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p304/r1.anchor: ومعلوم أنك أيها المتكلم لست تقصد أن تعلم السامع معاني الكلم المفردة التي تكلمه بها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p304/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p304/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p304/r2.claim: A sentence's subject, object, time, manner, and purpose depend on the verb's relation to its agent, together forming one unified communicated meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p304/r2.anchor: وهو إثباتك زيدا فاعلا ضربا لعمرو ، في وقت كذا ، وعلى صفة كذا ، ولغرض كذا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r1.claim: Descriptions such as متمكن and قلق apply to a whole word, not to its individual letters.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r1.anchor: متمكن ، أو قلق وصف للكلمة بأسرها ، لا حرف حرف منها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r2.claim: Saying that wording exceeds its meaning does not describe an isolated word or sentence; it describes adding an unnecessary signification while using one meaning to indicate another.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r2.anchor: وإنما فضل اللفظ عن المعنى أن تريد الدلالة بمعنى على معنى ، فتدخل في أثناء ذلك شيئا لا حاجة بالمعنى المدلول عليه إليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r3.claim: The analogous terms سبك and طابع also concern relations of signification, not the sound or wording considered by itself.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r3.anchor: وكذلك السبيل ي السبك والطابع وأشباههما لا يحتمل شيء من ذلك أن يكون المراد به اللفظ من حيث هو لفظ

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r4.claim: He condemns the entrenched habit of accepting claims about wording without examining them, saying it blocks attentive reasoning and leads to deceptive conclusions.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p331/r4.anchor: أن تركهم ، وكأنهم إذا نوظروا فيه أخذوا عن أنفسهم ، وغيبوا عن عقولهم

DAMGHANI:v1p100/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p100/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p100/r2.claim: جبار can mean a killer who acts unjustly; the accusation against Moses is that he would be such a killer.
DAMGHANI:v1p100/r2.anchor: الجبار القتال في غير حق قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء وإذا بطشتم بطشتم جبارين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r3.claim: The words You are plainly misguided may be spoken by the Israelite, blaming Moses for having killed a man while helping him the previous day.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r3.anchor: {قال له موسى إنك لغوي مبين} يجوز أن يكون هذا القول للإسرائيلي (1) . أي أغويتني بالأمس حتى قتلت بنصرتك رجلا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r4.claim: Alternatively, the words may be spoken by the man who was Moses and the Israelite's enemy.

NAHHAS:v3p232/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p232/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p232/r14.claim: The particle an is extra and serves emphasis.

NAHHAS:v3p232/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p232/r15.speaker: يزيد بن القعقاع
NAHHAS:v3p232/r15.claim: Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ reads yabṭishu with ḍamma on its initial letter; this is an attested dialect, though yabṭisha is more familiar and ḍamma is more analogical for an intransitive verb.
NAHHAS:v3p232/r15.anchor: وقرأ يزيد بن القعقاع ( أن يبطش ) وهي لغة إلا أن ( يبطش ) أعرف منها وإن كان الضم أقيس

NAHHAS:v3p232/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p232/r16.speaker: عكرمة
NAHHAS:v3p232/r16.claim: Ikrima says a person is not a tyrant until he has killed two people.
NAHHAS:v3p232/r16.anchor: قال عكرمة لا يكون الإنسان جبارا حتى يقتل نفسين

NAHHAS:v3p232/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p232/r17.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p232/r17.claim: Abū Isḥāq defines a jabbar as an arrogant person who refuses to submit to God's command.
NAHHAS:v3p232/r17.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الجبار في اللغة المتعظم الذي لا يخضع لأمر الله

NAHHAS:v3p232/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p232/r18.speaker: عكرمة
NAHHAS:v3p232/r18.claim: Ikrima's reading of the tyrant as a killer of two is compared with ʿAṭāʾ's warning that one must not assist, write for, or accompany an oppressor; he told a petitioner to discard his pen and seek God's provision.
NAHHAS:v3p232/r18.anchor: كما تأول عطاء فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين على أنه لا يحل لأحد أن يعين ظالما

NAHHAS:v3p232/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p232/r19.speaker: عطاء
NAHHAS:v3p232/r19.claim: ʿAṭāʾ advised a petitioner not to help wrongdoers, including by writing for or accompanying them, and told him to throw away his pen and seek God's provision.
NAHHAS:v3p232/r19.anchor: حتى قال لمن استفتاه ارم قلمك واسترزق الله جل وعز ولا تكن ظهيرا للمجرمين

SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r1.claim: The two pronouns in the clause apparently refer to Mūsā.

SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r2.claim: An alternative takes the pronouns as the Israelite and the Egyptian enemy; the Israelite, mistaking Mūsā’s movement as aggression, speaks, spreading the news while the killer remained uncertain.
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r2.anchor: وقيل: للإسرائيلي والعدو هو القبطي. والضمير في " قال يا موسى " للإسرائيلي

SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r3.claim: An is regularly extra after lammā, as here, and before law when preceded by an oath.
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r3.anchor: و " أن " تطرد زيادتها في موضعين، أحدهما: بعد " لما " كهذه

SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r4.claim: One cited poetic line attests extra an before wāw after an oath.
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r4.anchor: أما والله أن و كنت حرا

SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r5.claim: A second poetic line attests extra an before law after an oath.

SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r6.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r6.claim: The common reading has yibṭishu with kasra on the ṭāʾ.

SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:28:19/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads yabṭushu with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ.

ASAD-NOTES:28:19#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:19#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:19#n19/r1.claim: Moses is again swayed by kinship with the Israelite, whom he and the Israelite see as their common enemy.
ASAD-NOTES:28:19#n19/r1.anchor: swayed once again by his feeling of kinship with the Israelite

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p396/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p396/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p396/r1.claim: Bint tentatively suggests that fulk may connect the ship with falak in passages about divine power and cosmic order, rather than mean only a watercraft.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p396/r1.anchor: فهل يكون الفلك ما يربطها بالفلك في آيات القدرة الإلهية والنظام الكوني، وتكون السفينة لمجرد المركب المائي؟ ذلك ما ألمحه من بعيد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p396/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p396/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p396/r2.claim: Although glossing mashḥūn as filled is close, she hears shahn as suggesting the vessel's maximum capacity, with pressure and crowding.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p396/r2.anchor: وكذلك تفسير المشحون بالممتلئ، قريب، وإن كنت ألمح في الشحنة حس الدلالة على أقصى ما تحتمله الفلك من امتلاء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f13.claim: The added أن and separation after لما portray Moses as pausing before his second attempt to strike; the first incident instead uses successive fa clauses for immediate action.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f14.claim: Moses first rebukes his companion as plainly misguided; the companion then fears Moses means to strike him, supporting the author's reading that Moses was not rushing into action.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f14.anchor: ومما يدلك على تمهله وعدم اندفاعه في المرة الثانية تعنيفه لصحابه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f15.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f15.claim: The author states a general principle: wording may be added in one place and omitted in another according to meaning and context, as the examples that follow illustrate.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#7/f15.anchor: كلمة أو أكثر في موضع، ولا يذكرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p921/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p921/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p921/r1.claim: Grammarians differ on whether لمّا is a particle or an adverb, but the author treats it as temporal, meaning ‘when.’
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p921/r1.anchor: قسم يرى أنها حرف وقسم يرى أنها ظرف لكن هي زمنية وتسمى حينية أي حينما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p921/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p921/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p921/r2.claim: Inserting أن signals that Moses paused before striking; this conveys deliberation, unlike the immediate sequence expressed by فـ in 28:15.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p921/r2.anchor: فجاءت (أن) للدلالة على أنه لم يكن مندفعا وللدلالة على الفاصل في الزمن

NASHR:v2p273/r17.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r17.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p273/r17.claim: Abu Jafar reads the ṭāʾ with ḍamma in all three forms of the root.
NASHR:v2p273/r17.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بضم الطاء في الثلاثة

NASHR:v2p273/r18.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r18.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p273/r18.claim: The remaining readers read the ṭāʾ with kasra in all three forms.

QIRAAT-ER:28:19:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:19:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:19:6#1/r1.claim: A canonical u-vowel form varies the Form I imperfect dialectally; both forms mean violent seizure, though some grammatical analyses hear greater emphasis in the ḍamma form.
QIRAAT-ER:28:19:6#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift i→u on the middle radical (fatḥa→ḍamma on the stem)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#3/r1.speaker: author
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#3/r1.claim: A nearby Copt heard the exchange between Moses and the man and disclosed it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#3/r1.anchor: وقبطي قريب منهما يسمعهما فأفشى عليهما قال

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r1.claim: Baṭsh means seizing or striking with force and dominance.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r2.claim: The indefinite ʿaduww intensifies the sense, marking formidable enmity; the wording is not put into a possessive construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r2.anchor: والتنوين في عدو للتفخيم أي عدو عظيم العداوة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r3.claim: The man Moses meant to strike was the Copt, since the Copts were especially hostile to the Israelites; another view says he was an enemy to both because he followed neither man's religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالذي هو عدو لهما القبطي وقد كان القبط أعظم الناس عداوة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r4.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read yabṭishu with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر ( يبطش ) بضم الطاء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most commentators say the Israelite man said this, supposing Moses meant to strike him rather than the Copt because Moses had called him misguided.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r5.anchor: قاله الإسرائيلي الذي يستصرخه على ما روي عن ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the Copt said it, inferring from Moses calling the Israelite misguided that the Israelite was the man who killed the Copt the previous day; al-Ālūsī says this is possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن : قاله القبطي الذي هو عدو لهما

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r7.claim: On al-Ḥasan's account, the Copt's enmity to the Israelite follows from oppressing him, and his disobedience to God makes him Moses' enemy; religious difference is another possible basis of enmity.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r7.anchor: بأن هذا الذي أراد عليه السلام أن يبطش به كان ظالما لمن استصرخه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī warns that the Torah is disregarded where it contradicts the Qurʾān or sound Sunna; elsewhere, like other Israelite reports, it is neither affirmed nor denied, though it may corroborate some details.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r8.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن هذ التوراة لا يلتفت اليها فيما يكذب القرآن أو السنة الصحيحة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r9.claim: The Torah's Moses narrative differs from the Qurʾānic account through additions and omissions; here it omits the believer from Pharaoh's family who comes to advise Moses and lacks support for the accusation of tyranny.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r9.anchor: وهي فيما عدا ذلك كسائر أخبار بني إسرائيل لا تصدق ولا تكذب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r10.claim: Jabbār is one who does whatever he wants by striking or killing without weighing outcomes; another gloss is an arrogant person who will not submit to God's command, with the word likened originally to a tall palm.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r10.anchor: وهو الذي يفعل كل ما يريد من الضرب والقتل ولا ينظر في العواقب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r11.speaker: الشعبي وعكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r11.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says whoever kills two people without right is a tyrant, citing this verse; Ibn Abī Ḥātim reports a similar statement from ʿIkrima.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p57#2/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن الشعبي أنه قال : من قتل رجلين أي بغير حق فهو جبار

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r1.claim: The reformers are those who settle disputes among people by using the better course.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r1.anchor: بين الناس فتدفع التخاصم بالتي هي أحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r2.claim: After this accusation spread to Pharaoh and his chiefs, they resolved to kill Moses; a believer from Pharaoh's family, his cousin, came to warn and advise him, leading into the next verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r2.anchor: ولما قال هذا انتشر الحديث وارتقى إلى فرعون وملائه فهموا بقتل موسى

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.claim: أمس answers متى by locating an event in time, whereas كم asks for a duration or count; a time expression may be raised or made accusative according to its syntactic use.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.anchor: وأما متى فإنما تريد بها أن يوقت لك وقتا ولا تريد بها

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.claim: When الليل والنهار والدهر والأبد serve as duration adverbs, they cover the whole named span; they cannot denote only one part, though extended usage can make them non-adverbial.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.anchor: قولك سير عليه الليل والنهار والدهر والأبد

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.claim: Month names can denote a counted total of days, but شهر رمضان or شهر ذي الحجة names a specific time and answers متى.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.anchor: وصفر وجمادى وسائر أسماء الشهور إلى ذى الحجة

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.claim: Temporal and spatial adverbs parallel each other: كم can ask for counted duration or distance, while متى and أين identify a time and place; non-adverbial uses may be raised.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.speaker: ابن الرقاع
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكمتىيسارعليه؟وهويجعلهظ.claim: Ibn al-Riqāʿ’s verse with الشتاء illustrates seasonal expressions used as time answers; such expressions can also be understood as counted durations.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.claim: In رأيته إياه نفسه, إياه is an appositive and نفسه is descriptive emphasis; after the completed verb, قائما is a circumstantial accusative rather than a predicate complement.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.anchor: فأما نفسه حين قلت رأيته إياه نفسه فوصف بمنزلة هو وإياه بدل

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.claim: The separating pronoun and an emphatic pronoun such as إياه substitute for one another, so Sībawayh rejects combining both in the same predicate construction.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.anchor: ويدلك على أن الفصل كالصفة أنه لا يستقيم

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.claim: Sībawayh says the separating pronoun is stronger with verbs than with إن and its sisters, where an intervening phrase can make إياك acceptable.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.anchor: واعلم أنها في الفعل أقوى منها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.claim: Al-Khalīl accepts إنك إياك خير منه as Arabic, although Sībawayh regards it as remote; Sībawayh accepts إياك when an intervening phrase occurs.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتهإياهنفسهوضربتهإياه.anchor: وكان الخليل يقول هى عربية إنك إياك خير منه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.claim: An interrogative alif may follow waw, as in أو أهو; waw does not precede the alif as هل does, and this Qur’anic construction functions like فاء.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.claim: When an interrogative is repeated after أو, the question must be restarted; if the second question presents an alternative after uncertainty, أم is the appropriate disjunctive particle.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.anchor: ثم أعدت حرفا من هذه الحروف لم يحسن الكلام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.claim: A question such as ألست أخانا أو صاحبنا may ask about a shared set of descriptions, while repeated لست clauses with أو can instead present alternatives.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالواوالتيتدخلعليهاألفالا.anchor: وإذا قلت ألست أخانا أو صاحبنا أو جليسنا

SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.claim: Verbs such as حسب and ظن take two objects when they report a certain or uncertain judgment: the first is judged, and the second states its condition.
SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.anchor: منعك أن تقتصر على أحد المفعولين ههنا أنك إنما أردت أن تبين

SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.claim: ظننت ذاك, خلت, and حسبت may stand alone because ذاك supplies the cognate notion of thinking; forms like خلت زيدا and أرى زيدا are not acceptable in this use.
SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.anchor: وأما ظننت ذاك فإنما جاز السكوت عليه لأنك قد تقول

SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسلكأنms015تقتصرعلىأحدالمفعول.claim: In ظننت به, باء is meaningful rather than redundant: it marks what is assigned to supposition, unlike the extra باء in كفى بالله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r1.claim: Moses felt compassion for the Israelite and reached to strike the Egyptian.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن موسى أدركته الرقة (1) بالإسرائيلي فمد يده ليبطش بالفرعوني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r2.claim: The Israelite thought Moses was about to strike him because Moses was angry and had called him plainly misguided.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r2.anchor: فظن الإسرائيلي أنه يريد أن يبطش به لما رأى من غضبه وسمع قوله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r3.claim: Here being a tyrant on earth means killing unjustly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r3.anchor: {إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض} بالقتل ظلما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r4.claim: The Egyptian heard the Israelite’s words, realized Moses had killed the Egyptian the previous day, informed Pharaoh, and Pharaoh ordered Moses killed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r4.anchor: فلما سمع القبطي ما قال الإسرائيلي علم أن موسى هوالذي قتل ذلك الفرعوني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh sent executioners after Moses, who took the main road.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فلما أرسل فرعون الذباحين لقتل موسى أخذوا الطريق الأعظم

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r1.claim: The enemy of both Moses and the Israelite was not of their religion, and the Egyptians were enemies of the Israelites.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r1.anchor: لموسى والإسرائيلي لأنه لم يكن على دينهما ولأن القبط كانوا أعداء لبني إسرائيل

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r2.speaker: الإسرائيلي
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r2.claim: One view says the Israelite spoke, having assumed Moses would strike him after Moses called him misguided.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r2.anchor: قاله الإسرائيلي لأنه لما سماه غويا ظن أنه يبطش عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r3.speaker: القبطي
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r3.claim: Another view says the Egyptian spoke, supposing Moses had killed an Egyptian the previous day on this Israelite's behalf.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r3.anchor: أو القبطي وكأنه توهم من قوله أنه الذي قتل القبطي بالأمس لهذا الإسرائيلي

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r4.claim: إن تريد here means ما تريد.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r4.anchor: ما تريد. { إلا أن تكون جبارا فى الأرض }

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r5.claim: A جبّار is one who dominates people and ignores the consequences.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r5.anchor: تطاول على الناس ولا تنظر في العواقب

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r6.claim: Moses is accused of not being among those who reconcile people and settle disputes by the better course.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r6.anchor: فتدفع التخاصم بالتي هي أحسن، ولما قال هذا انتشر الحديث

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r2.claim: After the fighting, the discourse turns from the more important call to consider the afterlife to worldly consequences of that violence.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر القتال وأتبعه ما هو الأهم من أمره بالنظر إلى الآخرة , ذكر ما تسبب عنه من أحوال الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r7.claim: Moses then comes near the two men to help the Israelite, immediately moving to answer his renewed cry.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r7.anchor: مشيرا بالفاء إلى المبادرة إلى إصراخه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r8.claim: The infinitival particle أن is retained to reinforce the sense of intention; Moses’ movement confirms that he meant to act.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r8.anchor: الحرف الذي أصله المصدر تأكيدا لمعنى الإرادة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r9.claim: Moses intends to seize the Egyptian forcefully to free the Israelite from him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r9.anchor: أي موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام { بالذي هو عدو لهما } أي من القبط بأخذه بعنف وسطوة لخلاص الإسرائيلي منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r10.claim: The one described as enemy to both is the Copt who is oppressing the Israelite.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r10.anchor: من القبط بأخذه بعنف وسطوة لخلاص الإسرائيلي منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r11.claim: The Israelite, not the Copt, speaks the accusation; the context shows he alone knew Moses had entered unseen by others.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r11.anchor: بدخول المدينة على حين غفلة من أنهم لم يره أحد غير الإسرائيلي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r12.claim: Seeing Moses approach angry and rebuke him, the Israelite assumes Moses means to attack him rather than his Coptic enemy.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r12.anchor: ظانا أنه ما دنا إلا يريد البطش به هو

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r13.claim: He names Moses directly to remove ambiguity while denouncing what he thinks is an objectionable attack.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r13.anchor: باسمه العلم دفعا لكل لبس منكر الفعلة الذي اعتقده

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r14.claim: By revealing knowledge only he possessed, the Israelite exposes Moses’ secret and intensifies the danger and accusation against him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r14.anchor: ولما نم عليه وأفشى ما لا يعلمه غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r15.claim: Here إن means ما, so the accusation means that Moses wants nothing except to become a tyrant.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r15.anchor: أي ما { تريد إلا أن تكون } أي كونا راسخا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r16.claim: Jabbār describes one who dominates and overpowers others.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r16.anchor: أي كونا راسخا { جبارا } اي قاهرا غالبا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r17.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r17.claim: Abu Hayyan says a tyrant’s characteristic is killing without right.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r17.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وشأن الجبار أن يقتل بغير حق

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r18.claim: The accusation portrays Moses as seeking to rule where no one stands above him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r18.anchor: أي التي تكون بها فلا يكون فوقك أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r19.claim: The Israelite denies that Moses is naturally among those who make peace, since a peacemaker would not kill in this way.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r19.anchor: فإن المصلح بين الناس لا يصل إلى القتل على هذه الصورة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r20.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says that even a king partial to his people should not punish without proof; Pharaoh had asked whether there was evidence against Moses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r20.anchor: كما ذكر ذلك في حديث المفتون الذي رواه أبو يعلى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r21.claim: After Moses killed the Copt, Egyptians suspected the Israelites; the Israelite’s disclosure made Moses’ involvement certain.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p473/r21.anchor: وكانوا - لما قتل ذلك القبطي - ظنوا في بني إسرائيل

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Moses's Israelite ally thought Moses meant to strike him; their enemy heard the accusation and reported Moses.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {فلما أن أراد أن يبطش} قال: ظن الذي من شيعته إنما يريده فذلك قوله {أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس}

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r2.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says whoever kills two men is a tyrant, citing Moses's accuser.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: من قتل رجلين فهو جبار ثم تلا هذه الآية {أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says a man does not become a tyrant until he has killed two people.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: لا يكون الرجل جبارا حتى يقتل نفسين

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r4.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r4.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni says the mark of tyrants is killing without right.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r4.anchor: عن أبي عمران الجوني قال: آية الجبابرة القتل بغير حق

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses saw the Israelite fighting another Egyptian the next day. Regretting the previous killing, Moses disliked the scene, grew angry at the Israelite, and meant to strike the Egyptian.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r1.anchor: وبه عن ابن عباس : فبينما هم يطوفون ولا يجدون ثبتا اذا موسى قد راى من الغد ذلك الاسرائيلي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Israelite mistook Moses’s anger for yesterday’s and feared Moses meant to kill him. He blurted out the killing reference, then the Egyptian reported it to his people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r2.anchor: وبه عن ابن عباس قال : فنظر الاسرائيلي إلى موسى بعد ما قال له ما قال ، فاذا هو غضبان كغضبه بالامس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses let the Israelite go, and the Copt spread the news that Moses had killed the man.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r3.anchor: عن السدي قال يا موسى اتريد ان تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالامس قال : فتركه موسى ، وذهب القبطي فافشى عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r4.speaker: عكرمة والشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says a man is not a tyrant until he has killed two people; al-Shaʿbī is reported to hold the same view.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r4.anchor: قال عكرمة : لا يكون الرجل جبارا حتى يقتل نفسين . وروي عن الشعبي مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r5.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r5.claim: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī calls unlawful killing the hallmark of tyrants.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2958/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا عمران الجوني يقول : في هذه الاية ان تريد الا ان تكون جبارا في الارض يقول : واية الجبابرة القتل بغير الحق

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959/r1.claim: Qatāda is also reported to identify unlawful killing as the mark of tyrants.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959/r1.anchor: وروي ، عن قتادة مثل ذلك . قوله تعالى : وما تريد ان تكون من المصلحين
