IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq explains that this is not how reform is done.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959/r2.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق وما تريد ان تكون من المصلحين اي ما هكذا يكون الاصلاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r3.claim: The definite article in al-ams replaces a possessive complement: yesterday in relation to that event, not the day before revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r3.anchor: والتعريف في ( الأمس ) عوض عن المضاف إليه ، أي بأمسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r7.claim: Batsh means seizing violently; here it refers to striking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r7.anchor: والبطش : الأخذ بالعنف ، والمراد به الضرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r8.claim: The apparent meaning is that the opponent was a Copt; he may be called enemy to both because his hostility toward the Israelite was public and oppression itself opposed Moses's purified nature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r8.anchor: وظاهر قوله { عدو لهما } أنه قبطي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r9.claim: The question is used as a rebuke or denial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r9.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في الإنكار . والجبار : الذي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r10.claim: A jabbar does whatever he wants to harm people and treats them harshly instead of gently; compare the usages at 14:15 and 19:32.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r10.anchor: والجبار : الذي يفعل ما يريد مما يضر بالناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r11.claim: The accusation is that Moses wants to avenge by force rather than reconcile the disputants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r11.anchor: والمعنى : إنك تحاول أن تكون متصرفا بالانتقام وبالشدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r12.claim: The Copt's words appear to warn Moses against striking him; an exchange followed, then a man came from the far end of the city.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p93/r12.anchor: ويظهر أن كلام القبطي زجر لموسى عن البطش به وصار بينهما حوارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r1.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r1.anchor: قرأ جمهور القراء «يبطش» ، وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r2.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Abū Jaʿfar read yabṭushu with ḍamma on ṭāʾ; both are language variants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر بضم الطاء وهما لغتان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r3.speaker: الإسرائيلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r3.claim: The Israelite conveyed the accusation to Moses in his language, then fled and exposed the killing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r3.anchor: فقال الإسرائيلي لموسى معنى الآية بلسانه وفر منه فشهر أمر القتيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r4.claim: A jabbar is like rulers who kill unjustly, explaining the Israelite’s charge and denial that Moses was a reformer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r4.anchor: والجبابرة شأنهم قتل الناس بغير حق فلذلك جعله الإسرائيلي كذلك ونفى عنه الإصلاح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r5.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says whoever kills two men is a jabbar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r5.anchor: قال الشعبي: من قتل رجلين فهو جبار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r6.claim: Once the killing became known, Pharaoh and his council decided to kill Moses; Pharaoh saw him as a threat and sent troops after him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r6.anchor: ولما اشتهر أن موسى قتل القتيل وكان قول الإسرائيلي يغلب على النفوس تصديقه على موسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r8.speaker: ابن جريج أو ابن أبي نجيح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī tentatively attributes to Ibn Jurayj or Ibn Abī Najīḥ the view that the Israelite meant to strike the Egyptian; Moses stopped him, so the Israelite feared and exposed Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r8.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن ابن جريج أو ابن أبي نجيح، شك الطبري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r9.claim: Moses’ remorse and repentance make it inconceivable that he intended to attack another Egyptian.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r9.anchor: وكان موسى من الندامة والتوبة في حد لا يتصور معه أن يريد البطش بهذا الفرعوني الآخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r1.claim: The one Moses was about to strike was the Egyptian Copt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r1.anchor: أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما أي بالقبطي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r2.claim: The speaker is the Israelite; Ibn al-Jawzi knows no disagreement among commentators on this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r2.anchor: هذا قول الإسرائيلي من غير خلاف علمناه بين المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r3.claim: The Israelite saw Moses angry after being called a manifest misleader and about to strike the Egyptian, so assumed Moses meant to strike him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r3.anchor: قالوا لما رأى الاسرائيلي غضب موسى عليه حين قال له إنك لغوي مبين ورآه قد هم أن يبطش بالفرعوني ظن أنه يريده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r4.claim: The Egyptians did not know who killed the Copt. They told Pharaoh an Israelite had killed one of them, and Pharaoh demanded the killer and a witness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r4.anchor: وكان قوم فرعون لم يعلموا من قاتل القبطي إلا أنهم أتوا إلى فرعون فقالوا إن بني إسرائيل قتلوا رجلا منا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r5.claim: On the second day the Egyptian learned from the Israelite's words that Moses had killed the man, informed Pharaoh, and Pharaoh ordered Moses killed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r5.anchor: انطلق القبطي إلى فرعون فأخبره أن موسى هو الذي قتل الرجل فأمر بقتل موسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r6.claim: A man loyal to Moses learned of Pharaoh's order and warned him, introducing the next verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210/r6.anchor: فعلم بذلك رجل من شيعة موسى فأتاه فأخبره فذلك قوله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi glosses جبار as قتّال, ‘killer’; the commentary says it was explained in Hud.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r4.anchor: فأما الجبار فقال السدي هو القتال وقد شرحناه في هود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r3.claim: Moses calls the Israelite manifestly misguided and persistently troublesome.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r4.claim: When Moses resolved to strike the Copt, the fearful, weak Israelite thought Moses meant to attack him and blurted out the murder from the day before, protesting that Moses wanted to be a tyrant rather than a reformer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r4.anchor: ثم عزم على البطش بذلك القبطي، فاعتقد الإسرائيلي لخوره وضعفه وذلته أن موسى إنما يريد قصده لما سمعه يقول ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r5.claim: Only Moses and the Israelite knew about the earlier killing; the Copt overheard the Israelite's words, reported them at Pharaoh's gate, and provoked Pharaoh to seek Moses' death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p225#2/r5.anchor: فلما سمعها ذلك القبطي لقفها من فمه، ثم ذهب بها إلى باب فرعون فألقاها عنده، فعلم بذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r5.claim: One view says Moses addressed the Israelite, who had misled him into killing a man the day before and was now trying to mislead him again.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أنه قال ذلك للإسرائيلي لأنه قد أغواه بالأمس حتى قتل من أجله رجلا ويريد أن يغويه ثانية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Moses addressed the Egyptian; the Israelite mistakenly thought the rebuke was directed at him and became afraid.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r6.anchor: الثاني : أنه قال ذلك للقبطي فظن الإسرائيلي أنه عناه فخافه , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r7.claim: The enemy of both Moses and the Israelite is the Egyptian, whom Moses was moved to strike out of compassion for the Israelite.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r7.anchor: وهو القبطي لأن موسى أخذته الرقة على الإسرائيلي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r8.claim: One explanation is that the Israelite saw Moses angry and heard him call him misguided, so feared that Moses meant to kill him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r8.anchor: رأى غضب موسى عليه وقوله إنك لغوي مبين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r9.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r9.claim: Yahya ibn Salam's explanation is that the Israelite feared Moses would kill the Egyptian and then the Israelite would be killed in retaliation, so he tried to stop Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r9.anchor: الثاني : أن الإسرائيلي خاف أن يكون موسى يقتل القبطي فيقتل به الإسرائيلي فقال ذلك دفعا لموسى عن قتله , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r10.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r10.claim: Yahya ibn Salam reports being told that the Israelite was the Samaritan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r10.anchor: قال يحيى : وبلغني أن هذا الإسرائيلي هو السامري .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r11.claim: The Israelite released the Egyptian, who spread the report that Moses had killed a man the previous day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r11.anchor: وخلى الإسرائيلي القبطي فانطلق القبطي وشاع أن المقتول بالأمس قتله موسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r12.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r12.claim: Al-Suddi glosses jabbār as a killer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r13.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r13.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni says a tyrant's defining sign is killing without right.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r13.anchor: قال أبو عمران الجوني : وآية الجبابرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r14.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r14.claim: ʿIkrima says a person is not a tyrant until he has killed two people without right.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r14.anchor: قال عكرمة : لا يكون الإنسان جبارا حتى يقتل نفسين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p242#2/r15.claim: Reform is not carried out in this manner.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r1.claim: The one Moses meant to strike was the Copt, described as hostile to Moses and the Israelite either because he did not share their religion or because the Copts were enemies of Israel.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r1.anchor: لموسى والإسرائيلي لأنه ليس على دينهما أو لأن القبط كانوا اعداء بني اسرائيل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r2.claim: The Israelite spoke, mistakenly thinking Moses meant to seize him rather than the Copt, after Moses had called him plainly astray.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r2.anchor: الإسرائيلي لموسى عليه السلام وقد توهم أنه أراد أخذه لا أخذ القبطي إذ قال له إنك لغوي مبين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r3.claim: Here jabbār means a killer who acts in anger.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r5.claim: The Israelite accuses Moses of not wanting to be among those who restrain their anger.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r6.claim: The killing was widely known, but the killer had been concealed; the Israelite's words revealed Moses to the Copt, who informed Pharaoh and prompted the plot to kill him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231/r6.anchor: أن قاتله موسى فأخبر فرعون فهموا بقتله

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r4.claim: أمس means the day before; when unprefixed it is built on kasra for the meeting of two vowelless letters, but normally becomes declinable with the article or a possessive suffix.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r4.anchor: وأمس لليوم الذي قبل يومك، وهو مبني على الكسر لالتقاء الساكنين

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r5.speaker: سيبويه وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r5.claim: Some Arabs keep أمس indeclinable even with the article in nominative position; poets may extend that treatment to genitive or accusative under poetic necessity.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r5.anchor: وحكى سيبويه وغيره أن من العرب من يجري أمس مجرى ما لا ينصرف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r6.claim: غوي can mean ruined or unsuccessful, since Moses was challenging someone he could not withstand; another gloss is clearly misguided, because the Egyptian's conduct had brought a death yesterday and another threatened today.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r6.anchor: والغوي الخائب أي لأنك تشاد من لا تطيقه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says Moses called the Egyptian clearly misguided for exploiting the Israelite and preparing to strike him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: إنما قال للقبطي: { إنك لغوي مبين } في استسخار هذا الإسرائيلي

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r8.claim: غوي is an intensive form from أغوى, used in the sense of the causative participle; it may also mean one who has gone astray.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r8.anchor: والغوي فعيل من أغوى يغوي، وهو بمعنى مغو

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r9.claim: The verb بطش has both a- and u-vowel forms; the u-vowel is more analogical because the verb is intransitive.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r9.anchor: يقال: بطش يبطش ويبطش والضم أقيس لأنه فعل لا يتعدى

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r10.speaker: ابن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r10.claim: Ibn Jubayr says Moses moved to strike the Egyptian, but the Israelite thought Moses meant him after the harsh rebuke; the Egyptian heard the words and spread them.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r10.anchor: قال ابن جبير. أراد موسى أن يبطش بالقبطي فتوهم الإسرائيلي أنه يريده

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r11.claim: Another account says the Israelite was about to strike the Egyptian, Moses stopped him, and the frightened Israelite thought Moses meant to kill him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r11.anchor: وقيل: أراد أن يبطش الإسرائيلي بالقبطي فنهاه موسى فخاف منه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r12.claim: إن تريد here means you want nothing except that.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r12.anchor: { إن تريد } أي ما تريد. { إلا أن تكون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r13.speaker: عكرمة والشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r13.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Shaʿbi define a tyrant here as someone who has killed two people unjustly.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r13.anchor: قال عكرمة والشعبي: لا يكون الإنسان جبارا حتى يقتل نفسين بغير حق

QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r14.claim: The people meant by reformers are those who reconcile disputes between people.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:18-19/r14.anchor: أي من الذين يصلحون بين الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r8.claim: A tyrant may mean one who beats and kills unjustly without considering consequences or choosing what is better, or an arrogant person who will not humble himself before God.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r8.anchor: وقيل: الجبار الذي يفعل ما يريده من الضرب والقتل بظلم
